rated_messages.input_message: One way to combat any urges is to keep your mouth busy - some people find that chewing sugar free gum, mints, or even a pen can be a good alternative.

Write down why you want to stop smoking to resist a craving. Remember, trying something to beat the urge is always better than doing nothing. Each time you resist a cig, you're one step closer to being tobacco-free.
What can you do right now to break the automatic habit of smoking to help you feel better? Pause. Close your eyes. And take 10 slow breaths.
Practice staying in this location without smoking. Just notice your urge. Practicing this will weaken this trigger with time. Just think of it as practice.
If you find sounds soothing, tune in to the soundtrack of nature, like crashing waves, the wind rustling through trees, or birds singing.
Instead of lighting up a cigarette, light a scented candle or burn some incense.
Craving a cig? Plan a fun activity you can do when you get home as a reward for not smoking.
Take a deep breath. Focus on today and the things you have accomplished. How many urges have you let pass? Give yourself some credit!
Instead of smoking, use the next two minutes to pay close attention to your senses. Notice what you see, hear, feel, taste, and smell. Urges are just one part of your experience.
